newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to lift ban on securitising property - paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan to lift ban on securitising property - paper.

text.p: The Japanese government plans to allow the securitisation of collateralised land used for commercial purposes as part of a set of measures to boost liquidity in the property market to be announced by the end of this month, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun daily said on Monday.
The paper said the measure would go into effect in April.

The package of measures to boost land liquidity is aimed at helping Japanese banks, which are struggling under the weight of heavy bad loans, many of which were made to the real estate sector and were backed up by property as collateral, analysts said.
The paper said the package is expected to contain deregulation of 12 rules and tax incentives aimed at improving land liquidity.

The package will also authorise securitisation within the next fiscal year of 500 billion yen in collateralised loans made by failed housing loan firms and which are now administered by a special body.
The paper said Nikko Securities Co would lead-manage five monthly issues of around 100 billion yen each to securitise the collateralised loans made by failed housing loan firms.

The paper said other plans include legislation allowing for the establishment of special purpose companies to take over foreclosed property, and to issue bonds. The Finance Ministry is considering exempting special purpose companies from corporate taxes and taxes on the acquisition of property, it added.
